approved: International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Bill 2013

Proposed a supplementary bill making consequential changes to the Air Services Act, Civil Aviation Act and Personal Property Securities Act to support Australia's accession to the Cape Town Convention, preserving Airservices Australia's priority lien over unpaid charges and giving the Civil Aviation Safety Authority a new role recording aircraft deregistration and export authorisations.

Supported the International Interests in Mobile Equipment (Cape Town Convention) Bill 2013, noting the convention, in force since 1 March 2006 and ratified by 51 states, would let Australian airlines access a 10 per cent export finance discount under a 2007 OECD agreement, potentially saving as much as $2½ million on an Airbus A380 purchase, and applies to aircraft carrying as few as eight passengers.

Thanked the opposition for supporting the Cape Town Convention bills, which he announced at the Regional Aviation Association of Australia conference on the Sunshine Coast, describing them as part of the government's national aviation policy white paper that would let Australian airlines upgrade more quickly to safer, more fuel-efficient fleets.
